balance.argument_a: The Quick-Quote is read off the card in seconds -- easily inside Cassidy's one-hour deadline (Appendix A) -- and, because it undercharges relative to the true recursive fee, it hands Cassidy a genuinely more competitive number in a room where a rival custodian is already circling. Marcus does not need Meridian's compliance-grade workpapers to defend a rate the pricing desk itself published and approved for exactly this AUC band.
balance.argument_b: The Full Ladder is exact -- not an estimate -- and is the only one of the two numbers Marcus could actually defend, tier by tier, to the client's own finance team or to Meridian's compliance desk months from now. Real precedent exists for what an indefensible or wrong custody-fee number costs a bank over time: a real custody bank paid over $88 million after years of undisclosed billing errors on custody-client expenses (Appendix F, S3). A quote that is off by a real, computable 13.32% every year, for the life of a multi-year custody relationship, is a real and recurring cost -- not a one-time rounding error.
balance.margin_basis: For the client's stated AUC (Appendix A, MA1), compute Option A's fee (Appendix B's flat rate x AUC) and Option B's fee (Appendix C's recursive tier-by-tier total). margin_pct = |Option A fee - Option B fee| / Option B fee x 100.
balance.margin_note: COMPUTED 2026-09-01 (case-research), verified by script. At AUC = $850,000,000 (MA1): Full Ladder (Option B, exact recursion) -- Tier 1: fee=$170,000.00, balance after=$849,830,000.00; Tier 2 (1.25bp on $849,830,000.00): fee=$106,228.75, balance after=$849,723,771.25; Tier 3 (0.75bp on $849,723,771.25): fee=$63,729.28, balance after=$849,660,041.97; Tier 4 (0.50bp on $849,660,041.97): fee=$42,483.00, balance after=$849,617,558.97. True total fee = $850,000,000 - $849,617,558.97 = $382,441.03. Quick-Quote (Option A) = $850,000,000 x 0.000390 = $331,500.00. Gap = $331,500.00 - $382,441.03 = -$50,941.03 (Option A undercharges). margin_pct = 50,941.03 / 382,441.03 x 100 = 13.32%. WINNER on raw dollar accuracy: Option B, The Full Ladder -- but the margin is comfortably under SPEC §2's ~20% cap, and both options remain genuinely defensible (see argument_a/argument_b): B wins on accuracy/defensibility, A wins on meeting the deadline and on competitive-quote pressure. Scale-invariance check (also verified by script, feeds D4): the Full Ladder's true effective rate is EXACTLY 1 - (1-0.0002)(1-0.000125)(1-0.000075)(1-0.00005) = 0.04499306... = 4.499306 basis points, a fixed percentage independent of AUC (a provable algebraic consequence of the recursive definition being homogeneous of degree 1 in B0). Re-ran the full computation at AUC = $300,000,000 and AUC = $1,200,000,000 (Appendix D): true fees $134,979.19 and $539,916.75 respectively, Quick-Quote fees $117,000.00 and $468,000.00 respectively -- margin_pct comes out to 13.32% at ALL THREE sizes (to 2 decimal places). This is the intended D4 finding: the Quick-Quote card's error is a fixed percentage problem baked into MA5 vs MA6, not something that improves or worsens with client size.

sensitivity_note: margin_pct (13.32%) is driven entirely by two Modeling Assumptions: MA5 (the Quick-Quote card's flat rate, 3.90 bp) and MA6 (the Full Ladder's four tier rates, which fix the true blended effective rate at exactly 4.499306 bp for any client size -- a provable, scale-invariant consequence of the recursive definition being homogeneous of degree 1 in the starting balance). Neither MA1 (client AUC) nor MA7 (comparison-client AUCs) affects margin_pct at all -- confirmed by computing the full recursion at three different AUC sizes and getting 13.32% every time (see balance.margin_note and sensitivity_model.py). This is itself the case's D4 teaching point: a flat-rate approximation error, when both the true schedule and the flat quote are linear in balance, is a fixed percentage problem, not one that gets better or worse with a bigger or smaller client.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA5 is explicitly flagged 'the case's real fulcrum' in case.md: 'Moving MA5 up or down directly moves margin_pct.' The Quick-Quote card's rate for this fictional custody bank/band cannot be sourced more precisely than the real disclosed 0.3875-7.0bp industry range it was chosen inside (Appendix E); running sensitivity_model.py directly (not through the generic Tier-2 harness, whose evaluate() dict uses a raw-dollar-gap convention that produces a degenerate -100% reading) shows quick_quote_rate_bp at -50%/+50% moves true margin_pct to 56.66%/30.02%, both above the SPEC cap -- this is the case's own documented, disclosed design lever, not a hidden instability.
